text.title: Inference Cost Unit Economics Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns observed when computing inference cost unit economics. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix keyed to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: Report leads with "$0.03 per request"; finance later finds the feature costs ten times that per resolved ticket; pricing was set on the wrong number.
antipattern.root-cause: Per-call cost is the easiest number to pull from logs, so it becomes the headline. Multi-call flows, retries and abandoned sessions are never summed to the outcome.
antipattern.fix: Recompute as total cost of all calls attributed to an outcome divided by successful outcomes. Demote cost per call to a supporting line.

antipattern.symptom: Prompt was shortened by a third; cost per outcome did not move. Retry share was never measured.
antipattern.root-cause: Each retry logs as its own successful call, so dashboards show volume growth, not waste. Nobody joins calls to the outcome they served.
antipattern.fix: Tag every call with attempt number and outcome id; report retry share per feature; when above 15%, fix the retry policy before touching the prompt.

antipattern.symptom: Reported token volume is roughly a third of what the provider invoice bills; the gap cannot be explained.
antipattern.root-cause: Tokens were estimated from message character counts, which omit the system prompt, tool schemas and injected retrieval context.
antipattern.fix: Log the provider `usage` object per call, keyed by model id, and compute from it. Reconcile the monthly total against the invoice.

antipattern.symptom: Two reports for consecutive quarters show margin moving 20 points with no change in traffic; the difference is a repriced model nobody recorded.
antipattern.root-cause: Prices were copied from memory or an old spreadsheet without model snapshot id or sheet date.
antipattern.fix: Pin provider, model id, sheet date and applied discount per price line; diff price sheets between reports before interpreting margin movement.

antipattern.symptom: Average cost per outcome looks healthy; a handful of power users each cost more than their subscription every month.
antipattern.root-cause: Only the mean was reported. Long-context and agent-loop sessions form a heavy tail that the mean blends away.
antipattern.fix: Report p50, p95 and mean over at least seven days; flag features where p95 exceeds 5x p50 and name the tail driver.

antipattern.symptom: Two analysts compute 40% and 85% margin for the same bundled feature; the argument is about arithmetic when it is about allocation.
antipattern.root-cause: Feature has no direct revenue line; each report silently chose a different allocation key or value proxy.
antipattern.fix: State the revenue basis per feature (attributed, allocation rule with key, or value proxy with derivation) next to every margin figure.
